function.name: lawsuit_search
function.description: Search for lawsuits related to a particular subject matter in a certain location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location to perform the search in.

subject.description: The subject matter of the lawsuits.

year.description: Optional. The year in which the lawsuit was filed. Default: 2024

message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas – Key Points** | Topic | Summary | |-------|---------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits are the maximum speed allowed.
• In rural interstate highways, the default limit is 75 mph unless posted otherwise.
• In urban areas, limits are typically 55 mph (or lower). | | **Seat‑belt & Child‑Safety** | • All drivers and passengers must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child safety seat or booster. | | **Cell‑Phone Use** | • Hand‑held phone use while driving is prohibited.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed. | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) of 0.08 % or higher is illegal.
• For commercial drivers, the limit is 0.04 %. | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • At uncontrolled intersections, the vehicle on the right has the right of way.
• Pedestrians have priority at crosswalks. | | **School Bus** | • Vehicles must stop when a school bus is loading/unloading children. | | **Lane‑Changing & Passing** | • Must signal and check mirrors/blind spots.
• Passing on the right is prohibited unless the driver is turning left. | | **Traffic Signals & Signs** | • Red means stop; green means go; yellow means proceed with caution.
• Stop signs require a full stop. | | **Parking** | • No parking in front of driveways, fire hydrants, or on sidewalks.
• Parking in a handicap space requires a valid permit. | | **Towing & Tow‑away** | • Vehicles must be towed from the roadway if they pose a hazard. | | **Vehicle Registration & Insurance** | • Must carry proof of registration and insurance. | | **Special Rules** | • “No‑stop” zones, “no‑passing” zones, and “no‑turn” zones are enforced.
• “One‑way” streets require vehicles to travel in the indicated direction. | **Where to Find Official Texts** - Texas Transportation Code (Title 7, Chapter 1) – the statutory source for all traffic laws. - Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV) – provides handbooks and updates. - Texas Highway Patrol – enforces traffic laws and publishes guidelines. **Common Enforcement Practices** - Speed cameras and radar guns are used on major highways. - Police may issue citations for violations such as speeding, seat‑belt non‑use, or cell‑phone use. - Repeat offenders may face license suspension or points added to their driving record. **Resources for Further Reading** - Texas DMV Driver Handbook (PDF) – includes a chapter on traffic laws. - Texas Transportation Code online – searchable by section. - Texas Highway Patrol website – offers safety tips and legal updates. If you need more specific details (e.g., statutes, recent amendments, or how to contest a ticket), let me know!
